survey: A single cowboy boot seen almost in side profile, toe pointing right, from a camera slightly above and a little in front. The tall shaft rises straight up, and its top rim shows a sliver of tan lining only at the front-right dip. A stitched seam marks where the vamp joins the shaft at the ankle. The foot runs right to a pointed toe on a flat dark outsole. The block heel shows its side face and a lit front face that angles toward the toe, which matches the slightly high, slightly front-on view. The sole and heel rest on one level ground line, and the toe lifts a little. A gold spur sticks out of the back of the heel counter as a straight rod. Its star rowel is seen face-on, which is correct, since a rowel turns in the plane of the boot's side. The rowel and the boot body agree on one camera. Verticals stay vertical.

errors.what: The heel's visible front face and the hint of lining say the camera is slightly above. At that height the opening should read as a narrow ellipse, with the far inner wall showing across the whole width. Instead the rim is drawn as a flat profile outline, and the lining shows only in a small notch at the front-right. The top is not seen from the same height as the heel.

errors.where: Spur shank where it meets the heel counter
errors.what: The spur arm is a straight rod that ends in a rounded cap in front of the boot's side. It does not curve around the back of the heel the way a real spur band hugs the counter. So it does not follow the curved surface it should rest on, and it reads as floating beside the boot rather than strapped to it.

fix: Viewed from slightly above, the boot's top opening is a narrow ellipse with the inner lining visible all around the rim. The spur's U-shaped heel band wraps around the back of the heel counter, following its curve, and the star rowel sits at the back of the heel.
